drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 74-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.7, creatinine 0.94, hemoglobin 13.3, lactate 1.2, platelets 302, sodium 141, wbc 13.7; vitals dbp 68-71, heart_rate 87-100, map 87-89, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 19-22, sbp 124-128, spo2 96-98, temp 37.7-38.5
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Blood cultures x2; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.93, hemoglobin 13.3, platelets 295, sodium 140, wbc 11.5; vitals dbp 67-71, heart_rate 82-87, map 87-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 123-129, spo2 96-98, temp 37.3-37.5
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 74-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
